query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Doping the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with a small amount of silicon (approximately 1–2 at.%) will promote the in situ formation of a resilient, lubricious silica-based tribolayer during sliding. This tribolayer is expected to lower both the coefficient of friction and wear rate across the temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–2 at.% Si doping during alloy synthesis
generation.conditions: Dry sliding conditions in ambient air; temperature range from ~25 °C up to 800 °C; load and sliding speed set to values typical for wear testing of high-entropy alloys
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent silica (SiO2) tribolayer on the worn surface
generation.mechanism: Silicon doping alters the surface oxidation behavior during sliding such that a thin silica-based film develops. At lower temperatures, limited oxidation produces a nascent lubricious film that reduces friction. At elevated temperatures up to 800 °C, enhanced oxidation leads to the growth of a stable silica scale that minimizes metal-to-metal contact, thereby reducing friction and wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Si-doped alloy will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate over the entire temperature span compared to the starting CoCrFeNi alloy.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, which tends to show poor tribological performance due to unstable oxide formation and higher friction/wear across the temperature range
generation.boundary: Tested under dry/ambient conditions with sliding loads and speeds representative of industrial tribological applications; performance specifically evaluated between room temperature and 800 °C
generation.uncertainty: The optimal silicon content and the stability/adherence of the silica tribolayer under prolonged cyclic loading remain uncertain. The effectiveness may also vary with environmental oxygen partial pressure and sliding conditions not covered in the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens: one set of standard CoCrFeNi alloy and a second set doped with 1–2 at.% Si. Conduct systematic sliding wear tests across the temperature range from 25 °C to 800 °C under identical, controlled dry sliding conditions. Monitor the evolution of surface oxide layers using in situ or post-test surface analysis techniques such as X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) combined with energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS).
measurements: Coefficient of friction as a function of temperature and sliding time
Wear rate (mass loss or wear track depth) across the temperature range
Characterization of the tribolayer thickness, composition, and morphology
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Si-doped alloy does not show a statistically significant decrease in friction coefficient and wear rate relative to the undoped CoCrFeNi alloy across the full temperature range, or if no coherent lubricious silica tribolayer is detected, then the hypothesized mechanism is falsified.
